title: Whole-Series Metadata Edit (recurrence_id=None) Preserves Valid Overrides and Updates In-Place

citations.verbatim_quote: By default, an occurrence inherits all properties from the main object except the start (or due) date-time, which is shifted to match the recurrence id LocalDateTime.  However, individual properties of the occurrence can be modified by a patch or multiple patches.
The recurrence override converts to the "recurrenceOverrides" property of the converted main component.  Its RECURRENCE-ID property value converts to the key in the "recurrenceOverrides" property.

The full range of calendar components specified by a recurrence set is referenced by referring to just the "UID" property value corresponding to the calendar component.  The "RECURRENCE-ID" property allows the reference to an individual instance within the recurrence set.

rationale: In RFC 8984 Section 4.3.5 and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Section 2.1.2, a recurring series consists of a main component and zero or more recurrenceOverrides keyed by RECURRENCE-ID, where each occurrence inherits base properties from the main object unless overridden. When a whole-series edit (recurrence_id=None) updates series-wide descriptive or status metadata without invalidating existing recurrence instances, the store must update the master component in place and preserve all valid RECURRENCE-ID override components rather than performing a whole-series delete that destroys sibling components or cascades to delete RELATED-TO child components. Non-schedule metadata updates explicitly provided in the patch apply across the series while preserving each valid override component's instance-specific schedule (dtstart, dtend, due, duration, recurrence_id, and rrule=None) as well as any unpatched override properties.
store_implication: When editing a series with recurrence_id=None: (1) the store MUST NOT execute a whole-series delete that removes sibling components sharing the UID or cascades to delete RELATED-TO child components; (2) the master component (recurrence_id is None) MUST be updated in place; (3) for each existing override component (uid == target_uid, recurrence_id is not None, and neither rrule nor rdate is present) whose recurrence_id remains a valid occurrence of the updated master series, the override component MUST be retained in the calendar, with only the non-schedule metadata fields explicitly present in the patch applied and its own instance-specific dtstart, dtend, due, duration, recurrence_id, rrule=None, and unpatched metadata properties preserved.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Editing summary, description, or location of a series with recurrence_id=None when a single-instance override exists at 20250503T090000: both the master component and the override component remain in the calendar, and the override retains its rescheduled start and end times.

Selective metadata patching: If an override has a custom summary ('Special standup') and the whole-series edit patches only location ('Room 101') without specifying summary in the patch, both master and override receive location='Room 101' while the override preserves its custom summary ('Special standup').

Updating status of a recurring VTODO series (e.g. status=COMPLETED) with recurrence_id=None when a single-instance override exists: both master and valid override components are updated in place without deleting either component.
If the master series has a subordinate component linked via RELATED-TO;RELTYPE=PARENT, editing the master series with recurrence_id=None must NOT delete the subordinate child component.

scenarios.name: edit_entire_series_summary_after_override_preserves_override_component
scenarios.description: Editing the summary of a 5-day recurring series when [override, master] are present updates both components in place and preserves all 5 occurrences in the timeline.

audit_notes: Verified +/- 40 lines around all three citations and updated RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.7 line window to L6676-6680 (where Section 3.8.4.7 UID actually appears, rather than Section 3.8.4.4 at L6406-6410).

Confirmed authority STORE_POLICY is appropriate: while motivated by RFC 8984 Section 4.3.5 property inheritance, in-place whole-series editing that preserves valid RECURRENCE-ID overrides, selectively propagates patched non-schedule metadata, and avoids cascading RELATED-TO deletion is a store API policy choice.
Harmonized scenario and store_implication with R-L2-005 (exdate=[] on master alongside RECURRENCE-ID override) and unwrapped top-level JSON object.
